name: JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE
description: Concurred, argued that the Pretrial Fairness Act is constitutional as applied, and the circuit court lacked authority to indefinitely detain the petitioner, as the Act does not violate the separation of powers clause.

name: JUSTICE NEVILLE
description: Concurred, argued that Spencer's 100-year sentence is not a de facto life sentence due to parole eligibility after 20 years, but he can still bring an as-applied challenge in postconviction proceedings.

name: Justice Overstreet
description: Dissented, argued that the majority should not have denied the motion based on laches and should have addressed the complaint's merits to ensure legislative redistricting plans conform to the Illinois Constitution.

name: Justice Holder White
description: Took no part in the decision.

name: O'BRIEN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the police officer's actions constituted an unreasonable warrantless search, and the evidence should have been suppressed.

name: Justice Neville
description: Concurred with the majority's reasoning and conclusions regarding constitutional violations but dissented on the majority's reliance on the lockstep doctrine, arguing that the court should interpret the Illinois Constitution independently.

name: JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE
description: Concurred, argued that while a blind guilty plea does not waive sentencing challenges, the petitioner's 40-year sentence was proportionate to the offense and did not violate the proportionate penalties clause.

name: Justice Rochford
description: Took no part in the decision.

name: JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE
description: Concurred, argued that section 1(f) is a statute of repose, section 1.1 applies prospectively, and this does not violate due process.

name: JUSTICE OVERSTREET
description: Concurred, argued that warrantless arrests based on probable cause via investigative alerts are constitutional and juvenile sentencing factors were adequately considered.

name: Justice Neville
description: Dissented, argued that warrantless arrests based on investigative alerts violate the Illinois Constitution and enable racially discriminatory practices.

name: JUSTICE ROCHFORD
description: Concurred, argued that the officer-suit exception applies only to prospective injunctive relief, not to claims for monetary awards to redress past wrongs, which fall under the Court of Claims' jurisdiction.

name: Justice Neville
description: Took no part in the decision.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE THEIS
description: Concurred, argued that the Act did not diminish constitutionally protected pension benefits or constitute a taking of private property, as the ability to vote for local pension board members and control fund investments are not protected benefits, and the Act does not impact monetary pension payments.

name: JUSTICE ROCHFORD
description: Concurred, argued that the Act's exemptions do not violate equal protection or special legislation because plaintiffs are not similarly situated to the exempt classes, and that plaintiffs waived their second amendment and three-readings claims.

name: JUSTICE HOLDER WHITE
description: Dissented, argued that the Act should be found unconstitutional in its entirety due to a clear violation of the three-readings rule, which undermines constitutional process and democratic norms.

name: JUSTICE OVERSTREET
description: Dissented, argued that the Act should be found unconstitutional in its entirety due to a clear violation of the three-readings rule.

name: JUSTICE O'BRIEN
description: Dissented, argued that the classifications in the legislation do not further its claimed purpose and thus violate the special legislation provision, as the plaintiffs are similarly situated to the exempted groups.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE THEIS
description: Concurred, argued that the Act's pretrial release provisions are constitutional and do not violate the bail clause, crime victims' rights clause, or separation of powers clause.

name: Justice O'Brien
description: Concurred, argued that the majority failed to adequately address the defendants' affirmative defense regarding plaintiffs' standing, but ultimately agreed with the constitutionality of the Act.

name: Justice Overstreet
description: Dissented, argued that the Act's abolishment of monetary bail directly violates the plain language of the constitution's bill of rights, specifically the vested rights of crime victims, and that the legislature impermissibly usurped the people's sovereign power.

name: JUSTICE ROCHFORD
description: Concurred, argued that the court's emergency orders tolling the speedy-trial statute were a valid exercise of its constitutional authority over court procedure and did not violate the separation-of-powers clause.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE THEIS
description: Concurred, argued that defendant did not receive ineffective assistance of counsel because his attorney's performance was not deficient and defendant failed to show prejudice, and that the right to be present does not extend to the striking and accepting of jurors.

name: Justice Neville
description: Concurred, argued that while defendant did not show ineffective assistance, hearings to exercise challenges to jurors do constitute a critical stage of a trial where the defendant has a constitutional right to be present.

name: Justice O'Brien
description: Concurred, argued that counsel was deficient in agreeing to a procedure where defendant was not present for juror challenges, as this is a critical stage, but affirmed because defendant could not establish prejudice.

name: Justice Holder White
description: Concurred, argued that counsel was deficient in agreeing to a procedure where defendant was not present for juror challenges, as this is a critical stage, but affirmed because defendant could not establish prejudice.

name: GARMAN JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the plain language of the Amendment is unambiguous and applies to all transportation-related moneys, including those from home-rule units, and that the County's interpretation is unreasonable.

name: JUSTICE THEIS
description: Dissented, argued that the Amendment is ambiguous and, when read with home-rule provisions, should apply only to state-imposed tax revenues, not home-rule unit revenues, to harmonize conflicting constitutional sections and respect voter intent.

name: OVERSTREET JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the complete failure to administer a trial oath to the jury is structural error, requiring automatic reversal because it deprives the defendant of a basic protection guaranteed by the state constitution and threatens the integrity of the judicial process.

name: Connors
description: Dissented, argued that the circuit court's admonishments and inquiries during voir dire were insufficient to cure the failure to administer a trial oath, which is structural error requiring automatic reversal.

name: JUSTICE GARMAN
description: Concurred, argued that the City's ordinance defining "catastrophic injury" and "injury" was inconsistent with state law and judicial precedent, and thus preempted.

name: JUSTICE CARTER
description: Concurred, argued that the appellate court improperly found the petitioner's sentence unconstitutional without a sufficiently developed evidentiary record and that the actual innocence claim requires reconsideration in light of new precedent.

name: Chief Justice Anne M. Burke
description: Concurred in remanding the actual innocence claim but dissented from remanding the proportionate penalties clause claim, arguing it is a facial challenge that should be rejected based on Harris and that the age line for criminal responsibility is a legislative policy determination.

name: Justice Michael J. Burke
description: Concurred in remanding the actual innocence claim but dissented from remanding the proportionate penalties clause claim, arguing the defendant failed to make a substantial showing of a constitutional violation and that the determination of a sentencing line between juveniles and adults is a matter of legislative policy.

name: Justice Overstreet
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, joining Justice Michael J. Burke's opinion.

name: THEIS, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the firearm and ammunition tax ordinances are unconstitutional under the uniformity clause because the relationship between the tax classification and the use of the tax proceeds is not sufficiently tied to the stated objective of ameliorating gun violence.

name: JUSTICE MICHAEL J. BURKE
description: Concurred, argued that the majority's analysis is problematic because it leaves open the possibility for a future, more narrowly tailored tax on firearms and ammunition, which would still violate the Illinois Constitution's provision that the right to bear arms is subject only to police power, not taxation.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE ANNE M. BURKE
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JUSTICE MICHAEL J. BURKE
description: Concurred, argued that the search for child pornography was lawful under the Fourth Amendment because the original warrant, though partially resolved by acquittal for sexual assault, still authorized a search for unauthorized video recording, and the child pornography was found in plain view during a search reasonably directed at that remaining purpose.

name: Justice Neville
description: Dissented, argued that the search violated McCavitt's constitutional and statutory rights because the July 24, 2013, search warrant was void 96 hours after its issuance, and McCavitt's acquittal restored his right to the immediate return of his property, making any subsequent search illegal.

name: JUSTICE THEIS
description: Concurred, argued that the venue provision for identity theft is constitutional as the offense is deemed committed where the victim's intangible identifying information is located, satisfying the constitutional mandate.

name: JUSTICE MICHAEL J. BURKE
description: Other, took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JUSTICE GARMAN
description: Concurred, argued that the traffic stop was unlawfully prolonged, violating the fourth amendment, and therefore Bass's conviction must be reversed and remanded for a new trial, vacating the appellate court's opinion on limited lockstep analysis and investigative alerts.

name: Chief Justice Anne M. Burke
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the traffic stop was unlawfully extended and the conviction should be reversed, but dissented from vacating the appellate court's holding that defendant's arrest violated article I, section 6 of the Illinois Constitution.

name: Justice Neville
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the traffic stop was unlawfully extended and the conviction should be reversed, but dissented from vacating the appellate court's holding that defendant's arrest was unconstitutional under the warrant clause of the Illinois Constitution, as constitutional review of investigative alerts is merited.
